title: On Requiring three men for the whole job
subtitle: 社区社会 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 社区社会（社会服务与人际沟通·社区与社会参与）
meta: 主题语境：社区社会（社会服务与人际沟通·社区与社会参与）　|　核心词汇：require　|　正文 362 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 require 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1965 the director ① required three men for the whole job without complaint, and every actor in the theatre said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three nights on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the director ② requires three men for the whole job with great care without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ require three men for the whole job at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ required three men for the whole job before — a line in the poster for August 1959 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Requiring three men for the whole job without complaint, the director said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the script at the far stage, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ require an answer by the end of the week with great care, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Require an answer by the end of the week at once and never mention it again.

By 1972 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the poster, and a new actor from the next theatre ⑧ requires an answer by the end of the week without complaint every night without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the stage, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ required three men for the whole job again when nobody else would.

⑩ To require three men for the whole job, my mother said in 1977, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the theatre remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the theatre forgets, somebody requires three men for the whole job with great care again and somebody must require three men for the whole job without complaint all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 需要（一般过去式 required three men for the whole job：1965 年导演头一回这样做，毫无怨言地）
B. v. 需要（一般现在 requires three men for the whole job：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 需要（不定式 to require three men for the whole job：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 需要（过去完成时 had required three men for the whole job：1959 年八月的戏报上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 需要（动名词 requiring three men for the whole job 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 要求（require an answer by the end of the week：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去要求要求周末前答复）
G. v. 要求（require an answer by the end of the week：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 需要（后段两处：新来的演员照例 requires an answer by the end of the week，而母亲又一次 required three men for the whole job）

answers.why: require 意为“需要”，1965 年导演毫无怨言地需要整件活得要三个人，那是戏院里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 required。
require 意为“需要”，自那以后导演小心翼翼地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 requires。
require 意为“需要”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯需要整件活得要三个人”，此处为不定式 to require three men for the whole job。
require 意为“需要”，戏报里 八月 那行字说明早在 1972 年之前就有人需要过，故用过去完成时 had required。
require 意为“需要”，导演说“需要整件活得要三个人这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 requiring three men for the whole job 作主语。
require 意为“要求”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去要求要求周末前答复”，should ever 之后用原形 require an answer by the end of the week。
require 意为“要求”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻要求要求周末前答复（require an answer by the end of the week at once），以后再也不要提起。
require 意为“需要”，新来的演员每个夜晚都照例要求要求周末前答复，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 requires。
require 意为“需要”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次毫无怨言地需要整件活得要三个人，用一般过去式 required 叙述。
require 意为“需要”，结尾那句是母亲 1977 年的话：要需要整件活得要三个人，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和戏院记住的那一件。

老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻要求要求周末前答复，以后再也不要提起。（require an answer by the end of the week，祈使句）

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 require 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1965 the director required three men for the whole job without complaint, and nobody in the theatre forgot it.
Even now the director requires three men for the whole job with great care whenever the theatre asks.
Requiring three men for the whole job without complaint, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever require an answer by the end of the week with great care, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new actor from the next theatre requires an answer by the end of the week without complaint every night, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother required three men for the whole job again, and the theatre remembered that half.
